Might as well..
What's the largest-capacity vampire you can have?
You may start with any vampire, infinite setup time, and full
cooperation from other players.

Another rule/hint: The capacity need not be permanent; it might
only be during a particular action.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Max capacity vampire: 9 + ((40+10*#Meth) * #Meth).
Total distinct library cards in all libraries: 2. One is a
Succubus Club. The rest are Camarilla Vitae Slaves.

For five player games, the max library size is 90, so the max
capacity is 9+(90*5) = 459.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Chuck Arnett wrote:
>>>Max capacity vampire: 9 + ((40+10*#Meth) * #Meth).
>>>Total distinct library cards in all libraries: 2. One is a
>>>Succubus Club. The rest are Camarilla Vitae Slaves.
>>
>>>For five player games, the max library size is 90, so the max
>>>capacity is 9+(90*5) = 459.
>
> -1 for sucubus club?

Yes. That's why it's not 10+(90*5) = 460.

> 5 players with camarillia vitae slaves as all there library cards 450

Yes. But one of yours is a Succubus Club, so you get 449. Coupled
with your 10 capacity Lasombra, that makes 459 capacity.

> You have a Arika and Agritas, scholar of antiquity Agritas to draw off
> preys deck until he runs out they oast him and repeat.
>
> 450 cvs plus 11 cap = 461

But Arika cannot play the Camarilla Vitae Slave. So you either need a
Clan Impersonation or use a 10-cap Lasombra instead. Either way will get
you 460 (since the use of Agaitas saves you a card slot by eliminating
the Succubus Club).

Unfortunately, this doesn't work, since each other player will have
drawn 7 cards (7 Camarilla Vitae Slaves) that you cannot touch with
Agaitas. So your max capacity drops by 7*4 = 28, making 432.

So the max remains at 459, using Succubus Club.

> but I would do 460 and put a Golconda in my deck :)

With Golconda in the deck as well, you'd only reach 458 capacity.
